title: Build your own Redis
about: Learn how Redis works by building one in C++20: the RESP protocol, a single-threaded kqueue event loop, the keyspace and its data structures, expiry, eviction, persistence, replication and messaging. The milestones are servers that redis-cli and redis-benchmark talk to unchanged, checked against replies recorded from real Redis. Run `python3 tools/sync_curriculum.py` after every edit. Rule: an exercise depends only on exercises at its level or below.

levels.name: Basic
levels.meaning: the protocol, the command table and a blocking server: talk to redis-cli

levels.name: Intermediate
levels.meaning: the event loop and the real keyspace: a usable mini Redis

levels.name: Advanced
levels.meaning: compact encodings, eviction, persistence, replication, messaging

tracks.name: Protocol
tracks.goal: speak RESP and serve redis-cli from a blocking server

tracks.name: Event loop
tracks.goal: serve thousands of clients from one thread, the way ae.c does

tracks.name: Keyspace
tracks.goal: Redis's data model: dict with incremental rehash, typed values, expiry, SCAN

tracks.name: Internals
tracks.goal: why Redis is small and fast: skiplists, listpacks, intsets, approximate LRU

tracks.name: Durability
tracks.goal: survive kill -9 and keep a replica in sync: RDB, AOF, PSYNC

tracks.name: Messaging
tracks.goal: clients talking to clients: pub/sub, transactions, blocking pops

exercises.title: RESP encoder
exercises.about: the five RESP2 types on the wire: simple strings, errors, integers, bulk strings, arrays, and the two nulls

exercises.title: Incremental RESP parser
exercises.about: parse requests that arrive in arbitrary fragments; 'need more bytes' is a result, not an error; inline commands (optional)

exercises.title: Command table
exercises.about: case-insensitive lookup, arity checks and Redis's exact error strings, the way server.c's command table works

exercises.title: String commands
exercises.about: GET/SET (NX/XX/GET), DEL, EXISTS, INCR/DECRBY, APPEND, MGET/MSET on a plain map; 64-bit overflow is an error

exercises.title: Glob matching
exercises.about: Redis's stringmatchlen: *, ?, [a-z], [^x], escapes; and why the naive backtracker is exponential

exercises.title: Blocking sockets
exercises.about: socket/bind/listen/accept, short reads and short writes, SO_REUSEADDR, SIGPIPE; an echo server

exercises.title: CRC-64 (Jones)
exercises.about: the checksum at the end of every RDB file: bit-by-bit, then table-driven

exercises.title: Hello, redis-cli
exercises.about: a blocking one-client-at-a-time server; redis-cli connects and PING, ECHO, SET, GET, INCR work

exercises.title: I/O buffers
exercises.about: growable read/write buffers with cheap consume-from-front; amortised compaction instead of memmove per command

exercises.title: Non-blocking I/O
exercises.about: O_NONBLOCK, EAGAIN, partial writes and connect-in-progress; read until EAGAIN, write what the kernel takes

exercises.title: Timer events
exercises.about: a min-heap of deadlines with cancellation; how long the loop may sleep; tested with a fake clock

exercises.title: kqueue event loop
exercises.about: Redis's ae.c on kqueue: readable/writable file events, time events, beforeSleep, and deleting a handler while it runs

exercises.title: Client state machine
exercises.about: query buffer, pipelining, reply buffer, write-when-writable, query-buffer limits and closing a client mid-batch

exercises.title: Event-driven server
exercises.about: one thread, many clients: redis-benchmark -c 50 -P 16 -t ping,set,get runs clean

exercises.title: Dict with incremental rehash
exercises.about: Redis's dict.c: chained buckets, power-of-two tables, rehashing a few buckets per operation so no command ever stalls

exercises.title: SCAN cursors
exercises.about: reverse-binary cursor increments: every key present for the whole scan is returned, even while the table grows or shrinks

exercises.title: Typed keyspace
exercises.about: move the strings onto your dict; typed values, WRONGTYPE, TYPE, OBJECT ENCODING; lookups that will later expire and track LRU

exercises.title: Expiry
exercises.about: EXPIRE/PEXPIRE/TTL/PERSIST, SET EX; lazy expiry on access plus the active cycle that samples 20 keys and repeats while >25% are stale

exercises.title: Lists
exercises.about: LPUSH/RPUSH/LPOP/RPOP/LRANGE/LINDEX/LLEN/LTRIM; negative indices and out-of-range ranges; empty lists delete their key

exercises.title: Hashes
exercises.about: HSET/HGET/HDEL/HGETALL/HLEN/HINCRBY on your dict; a dict inside a dict

exercises.title: Sets
exercises.about: SADD/SREM/SISMEMBER/SMEMBERS/SCARD and SINTER/SUNION/SDIFF (iterate the smallest set first)

exercises.title: Generic key commands
exercises.about: KEYS, SCAN MATCH COUNT TYPE, RENAME, DBSIZE, FLUSHDB, RANDOMKEY; why KEYS is banned in production and SCAN isn't

exercises.title: Mini Redis
exercises.about: the event server plus the full keyspace and an active-expiry cron; passes the compatibility suite recorded from real Redis

exercises.title: Skiplist with ranks
exercises.about: Redis's zskiplist: p=1/4 levels, backward pointers, span counts for O(log n) rank; deterministic levels for tests

exercises.title: Sorted sets
exercises.about: skiplist + dict: ZADD (NX/XX/GT/LT/INCR), ZSCORE, ZRANK, ZRANGE BYSCORE/REV/LIMIT; score formatting that matches Redis byte for byte

exercises.title: Intset
exercises.about: a sorted array of 16/32/64-bit integers that upgrades its encoding in place; binary search; little-endian on disk

exercises.title: Listpack
exercises.about: one contiguous allocation of variable-length entries with back-lengths for reverse walks; why it replaced ziplist (cascading updates)

exercises.title: Compact encodings
exercises.about: small hashes/sets/zsets/lists live in listpacks and intsets and convert past the *-max-listpack-* thresholds; OBJECT ENCODING matches real Redis

exercises.title: maxmemory and approximate LRU
exercises.about: memory accounting, a 24-bit LRU clock, sampling with an eviction pool of 16; allkeys-lru, volatile-ttl; LFU's log counter (optional)

exercises.title: Lean Redis
exercises.about: a leaderboard on sorted sets under maxmemory with eviction; redis-benchmark within 2x of real Redis, memory within 1.5x

exercises.title: RDB writer
exercises.about: the RDB format: length encoding, int-encoded strings, opcodes for expiry and SELECT, the CRC-64 trailer; real Redis must load your file

exercises.title: RDB reader
exercises.about: load dump.rdb files written by real Redis and by your writer; reject a bad checksum; skip already-expired keys

exercises.title: BGSAVE with fork
exercises.about: fork + copy-on-write snapshots, write to temp then rename, reap the child from a timer; why the parent must not rehash during a save

exercises.title: Append-only file
exercises.about: log writes as RESP, appendfsync always/everysec/no, replay on startup through your parser, recover from a truncated tail

exercises.title: AOF rewrite
exercises.about: compact the log from a forked snapshot while new writes keep arriving; swap files atomically

exercises.title: Replication backlog
exercises.about: a ring buffer addressed by global replication offset: can this replica resume from offset N, or does it need a full sync?

exercises.title: Replica and PSYNC
exercises.about: REPLICAOF: handshake, full sync by RDB transfer, then the live command stream; partial resync after a disconnect; REPLCONF ACK

exercises.title: Durable Redis
exercises.about: kill -9 loses at most a second of writes; real Redis loads your dump.rdb; your replica follows a real Redis primary

exercises.title: Pub/Sub
exercises.about: SUBSCRIBE/PSUBSCRIBE/PUBLISH/UNSUBSCRIBE, the restricted subscriber mode, and why a slow subscriber needs an output-buffer limit

exercises.title: MULTI/EXEC/WATCH
exercises.about: queued commands, EXECABORT on syntax errors vs runtime errors inside EXEC, optimistic locking with WATCH and touched keys

exercises.title: Blocking pops
exercises.about: BLPOP/BRPOP across several keys with timeouts; wake the longest waiter first; serve after the pushing command, not inside it

exercises.title: Messaging Redis
exercises.about: a chat over redis-cli SUBSCRIBE, a job queue with BLPOP workers, and a WATCH-guarded counter that never loses an increment

edges: see the format from the writing side first
replies are encoded to compare bytes
short reads are why buffers exist
partial writes stay in the buffer
parse every complete command in the query buffer
the string commands move onto your dict
a hash's fields live in a dict
only for RENAME keeps the TTL
active expiry runs as a time event
sorted sets in RDB are an optional section
reap the child from a time event
